newsitem.title: UK: Abattoirs making killing out of BSE - UK Liberals.
newsitem.headline: Abattoirs making killing out of BSE - UK Liberals.

text.p: Five big abattoir and rendering companies have made many millions of pounds in excess profits out of Britain's "mad cow" crisis, the agriculture spokesman of the minority Liberal Democrats said on Wednesday.

Paul Tyler told the party's annual conference in Brighton the government had given a "stunning example" of incompetence in their handling of the slaughter of cattle vulnerable to Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), or mad cow disease.
"Ministers decreed that the hugely profitable cattle cull should be left in the hands of a cosy little carve-up by the cartel of big abattoir and renderers groups," he said.
The government had now admitted the price paid to abattoirs to slaughter cattle -- 87.50 stg per animal -- was four times what its advisers thought economic, and payments had been cut.
"It is estimated that five companies have made many millions of excess profits as a result of this favouritism," Tyler told delegates. "Who is making a killing now?"

"Meanwhile smaller abattoirs have been driven out of business, the cull of over-30-month (old) cattle has been managed with inconceivable incompetence, the backlog of cows waiting on the farms is growing and specialist beef producers are on the brink of bankruptcy."

He blamed the government rather than the European Union for the crisis, saying cattle should have been culled years earlier to contain the disease, and that farm minister Douglas Hogg had shown "all the diplomatic finesse of a bull in a china shop".

The conference went on to debate an emergency motion urging the government to break the impasse over the export ban on British beef by submitting detailed proposals on how to proceed with a selective cull of cattle under 30 months to Brussels as soon as possible.
